title: GRU Gates: Keep or Update
tagline: The update gate is a learned dial between remembering the past and taking the new candidate
summary: A GRU cell decides, each step, how much old state to keep and how much to replace. Slide the update gate z and watch the new state h_t = (1−z)·h_{t-1} + z·h̃_t glide along a number line between the past and the candidate, with a keep-vs-update proportion bar making the interpolation literal. The reset gate r controls how much of the past the candidate can even see. A compact GRU-vs-LSTM table sits alongside: 2 gates and one merged state vs 3 gates and a separate cell.
highlights: Slide the update gate z and watch h_t interpolate along a number line between the past h_{t-1} and the candidate h̃_t.
See the update gate drawn as a keep-vs-update proportion bar — the interpolation made literal.
Turn the reset gate r and read the candidate's arithmetic update: tanh(x + r·h_{t-1}) with the numbers substituted.
Presets for copy-through (z=0), overwrite (z=1), and ignore-the-past (r=0) show the extremes at a click.
A compact GRU-vs-LSTM comparison: 2 gates and one merged state versus 3 gates and a separate cell state.
